newsitem.title: THAILAND: New Aspiration wins Thai poll narrowly - ministry.
newsitem.headline: New Aspiration wins Thai poll narrowly - ministry.

text.p: The Interior Ministry said officially on Monday that the New Aspiration Party (NAP), led by Defence Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, had won the Thai election by a razor-thin two-seat majority.

The ministry said the results showed that the NAP swept 125 seats in the 393-seat parliament against 123 won by it chief rival, the Democrat Party, led by former premier Chuan Leekpai in Sunday's very close polls.

Earlier, television stations had projected unofficially that the NAP would win by the 125-123 after a tight election race which analysts said was peppered heavily with violence and bribery. This poll was billed as the dirtiest in two decades.

After unofficial results were declared on television, Chavalit told a news conference, flanked by leaders of four other potential coalition partners, that he would be victorious. He and Chuan were not available for comment immediately.

As tradition dictates, the NAP will now have the right to form a new coalition government. The NAP's four allies, the Chart Thai, the Prachakorn Thai, the Social Action Party and the Muonchon Party contol a total of xx seats, which when combined with those won by the NAP, would give the group a majority of 204 seats in parliament.

Analysts said the financial markets were expected to adopt a wait and see attitude over the next few days to see what sort of coalition government would emerge with NAP at the helm. The markets had been expecting a Democrat Party win.
